articles.title: De Gaulle: Résistance review – a galloping bromance for Churchill and France’s wartime hero
articles.summary: This biopic of the great Gallic general – which culminates at Bir Hakeim, in advance of a second film – is a fine, quietly amusing romp with a touch of classic 60s war films.
body: Perhaps because it is based on a biography by an Englishman – Julian Jackson’s A Certain Idea of France: The Life of Charles de Gaulle – this very enjoyable and gallopingly eventful biopic, directed by Antonin Baudry, has an element of amused detachment. The first of two parts, it offers a good-humoured, though naturally sympathetic, perspective on France’s great wartime hero, played with martyred and faintly preposterous hauteur by Franco-Armenian actor Simon Abkarian.

Then, we get the high comedy of De Gaulle’s chaotic personal adventures in Africa, finding support for his Free French in Chad and Cameroon, which Churchill admires as audacious if absurd. But Africa is important. An Anglo-Hollywood movie might have seen Britain’s turning point in the war as a matter of dramatising Montgomery’s brilliance at El-Alamein. This French movie instead emphasises the heroism of an outnumbered Free French brigade in the desert at Bir Hakeim under Gen Marie-Pierre Kœnig (Benoît Magimel); inspired by De Gaulle, they hold out against Rommel’s superior forces, giving British forces a chance to retreat and regroup.
points: This biopic of the great Gallic general – which culminates at Bir Hakeim, in advance of a second film – is a fine, quietly amusing romp with a touch of classic 60s war films.

articles.title: Venice-Selected ‘Agata the Writer,’ Starring Mia Wasikowska, Boarded by MMM Film Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: French sales company MMM Film Sales has acquired the international rights to “Agata the Writer,” starring Mia Wasikowska, which will have its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival in the Venice Days section, in competition.
body: The Australian film is directed by filmmaker and artist Kuba Dorabialski, and is produced by Alex White, best known for “Babyteeth.”

The MMM Film Sales team said, “We were immediately drawn to ‘Agata the Writer’ for its unique voice and its fascinating reflection on how we engage with history and memory. Mia Wasikowska perfectly embodies the role of Agata, a writer returning to her home continent, seeking to understand and reconnect with the wounds of the recent past, and with the ways in which unresolved conflicts continue to echo in the present. Kuba Dorabialski has crafted a film that is both playful and thought-provoking, questioning the relationship between storytelling, identity and responsibility.”

“Agata the Writer” is a Whitefalk Films and Produktion Productions film. Principal production funding came from Screen Australia. It is financed with support from Creative Australia and the Adelaide Film Festival Investment Fund.

articles.title: GameSquare Pivots Livestreaming Measurement Service Stream Hatchet Into Creator Marketing Analytics Platform (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: GameSquare is rebranding its gaming and esports-focused livestreaming measurement platform Stream Hatchet into Hatchet, which it describes as “the first full-service creator matching and brand marketing analytics platform built for marketers looking to engage in youth culture with an emphasis on…
body: The new creator marketing analytics solution aims to help brands leverage the impact of gaming on youth culture.

“What we are doing with Hatchet is truly unique. This is not a generic tool being retrofitted to gaming. It is a full-service proposition backed by the entire GameSquare ecosystem,” GameSquare CEO Justin Kenna said. “The goal here is to help brands live and thrive at the center of a core aspect of youth culture — gaming. For comparison, we are building something that gives the same type of insights as the Nielsen ratings, but for content creators and using the highest standard that exists in the market, with more options than other platforms offer.”

“Over the years Hatchet has developed powerful tools and data sets to move the industry past reactive discovery,” Hatchet director of product Alessandra Pinto said. “Brands and publishers need an extension of their team, one that is continuously learning from performance patterns, surfacing opportunities, and tuning itself to their needs. Hatchet is our vision as that true strategic partner to help brands move from outreach to activation and manage the full campaign life cycle.”

articles.title: COL Group, CP Group Strike 360-Degree Partnership to Grow Thailand’s Short-Form Drama Industry
articles.summary: COL Group and CP Group are teaming on a partnership aimed at building up Thailand’s short-form drama business, linking creative training, local content production and distribution under a single initiative.
body: The deal centers on a talent incubation program the two firms will run jointly with an academic institution in Thailand, aimed at connecting new creative talent with the short-form entertainment sector. The companies said the effort is meant to widen the pipeline of talent feeding Thailand’s entertainment industry over time.

On the distribution side, FlareFlow will get a dedicated branded corner inside Tatang by TrueID, the short-form drama app run by True Corporation, part of CP Group. Called FlareFlow Mini, the corner is set to launch in September and will house FlareFlow’s vertical-drama catalogue for Thai audiences, with new titles added weekly.

articles.summary: “Alice and Steve” has been picked up for a second season at Disney+ and Hulu. The comedy — which airs on Disney+ in the U.K. and Ireland and on Disney+ and Hulu in the U.S.
body: “I am so thrilled that ‘Alice and Steve’ has been given a second season,” creator and writer Sophie Goodhart said in a statement. “No one will be prepared for what happens next, especially not Alice and Steve.”

“Alice and Steve” is executive produced by Petra Fried, Sophie Gardiner and Wim de Greef, with co-executive producer Rachael Stephenson for Clerkenwell Films, which is part of BBC Studios. The series was commissioned by Lee Mason, VP of scripted at Disney+ EMEA.

“We absolutely love ‘Alice and Steve’ — both the show and of course the two characters at the heart of Sophie’s brilliantly messy, funny and fearless exploration of friendship and love,” Fried said. “We’re thrilled to be bringing it back for a second season and can’t wait for audiences to see what Sophie has in store for our favorite frenemies.”

articles.title: How Dolly Parton helped the world - from children's books to supporting Covid vaccine
articles.summary: The late singer-songwriter's charity causes were as eclectic as her music, but she had a personal connection to each one.
body: Dolly Parton will not only be remembered for her iconic songs and Southern charm, but also for her philanthropic work.

Throughout her life, she supported communities in need, especially in her home state of Tennessee. She funded medical research that led to one of the first Covid-19 vaccines, donated to wildfire victims and even helped the once-endangered bald eagle, America's national bird.
But it is her Imagination Library - the mainstay of her charity work - that has helped millions of children learn to read by sending out free books.
The programme was inspired by her father who couldn't read or write.

articles.title: Heart, hope and a steely determination: Dolly Parton's musical legacy
articles.summary: BBC music correspondent Mark Savage looks back on the legacy of the "irreplaceable" late singer.
body: In 1980, Dolly Parton was filming her first Hollywood movie, 9 To 5, and between scenes she had an idea for the tune that would become the movie's theme song.
But her guitar was banned from the set - so she made the beat by strumming her acrylic nails together.
The sound, she realised, was just like the typewriter used by her character, a married secretary who is constantly belittled and sexually harassed by her boss.
Excited, she ran over and sang the song to her co-stars Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda, who was also the film's producer.

articles.title: The Last Sunrise review – Amazon’s soapy YA romance is thankless and bland
articles.summary: Another familiar concoction fails to make use of its sunny location and chooses cheap melodrama over romantic charm. A titular sunrise, a summer fling fantasy, exorbitant wealth, impossibly sculpted bodies: such are the profitable story ingredients that make up The Last Sunrise, the latest offering…
body: Oh, right: money. In recent years, romance – which has long been maligned as an “unserious” genre – has regained prominence in the cultural spotlight. The romcom died and was reborn as steamy television; commercial romance fiction filled with graphic detail. But as the genre returns to its position as a pillar of the entertainment industry, the human-scale simplicity that gave us Bridget Jones’s Diary has been neglected and replaced by half-baked efforts like The Last Sunrise – the main value of which is to expose, all too clearly, how indifferently streaming platforms regard their audience.

articles.title: Taylor Swift and Beyoncé lead tributes after death of 'bold and brilliant' Dolly Parton
articles.summary: Tributes pour in from across the worlds of music, film and politics for the star, who has died at 80.
body: Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, Sir Paul McCartney and Sir Elton John have led an outpouring of tributes from celebrities and fans to Dolly Parton following the music icon's death at the age of 80.
Swift said Parton's "legacy will be an everlasting one", while Beatles legend Sir Paul called her a "magnificent star".
The Tennessee-born singer and songwriter died on Tuesday at the age of 80 after "a brief battle with cancer", her team said in a statement.

Parton is known for iconic songs including Jolene, 9 to 5 and I Will Always Love You. She was also an actress and philanthropist, who helped fund one of the first Covid-19 vaccines and poured millions into improving children's literacy.

articles.title: Hanging By a Wire review – cable car rescue documentary dangles viewers on the edge of disaster
articles.summary: The extraordinary fate of eight people trapped above a chasm in Pakistan makes for a tense, skilfully assembled survival story with unexpected flashes of comedy. Survival documentaries are a weird little genre of nonfiction film-making that recount the stories of accidents and natural catastrophes…
body: Credit is due to director Mohammed Ali Naqvi for pulling it all together adeptly, as well as to the seamless editing by William Grayburn that nourishes the suspense and draws out some of the surprising moments of comedy. It’s good to have a bit of a giggle amid all the tension; we meet one heroic zip line enthusiast who brags about his amazing body as he struts around the gym he runs, looking buff but not outrageously so. The fact that he’s introduced halfway through the story lets us know he’ll survive, as will his best buddy, who has a lot less braggadocio.

articles.title: 'If you want the rainbow, you gotta put up with the rain': The wit and wisdom of Dolly Parton
articles.summary: The much-loved country singer-songwriter in her own words, following her death aged 80.
body: Dolly Parton, the much-loved US singer-songwriter who has died at the age of 80, was known for her pearls of wisdom and humour as well as her music.
She regularly offered her perceptive and witty insights about life, music, fame and equal rights.
"The way I see it, if you want the rainbow, you gotta put up with the rain."
"I always just thought if you see somebody without a smile, give 'em yours!"
